subject: Planning: multi-region demo series — avoid Golden Week / Diwali / Easter conflicts

Subject: Request: single demo or a short series (May availability)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the intro — we'd like to set up a product walkthrough for our cross-regional infrastructure and inference use cases. We have stakeholders in the US, UK/EU and Japan/India. The initial ask from our side: a 60–90 minute demo + Q&A and a shorter follow-up technical deep-dive for our infra team. Ideally we'd schedule the first session in early May (week of May 2–13) so the PMs can attend before their Q2 planning.

Quick constraints:
- Our India team expects Diwali-related OOO windows in November, so they're flexible for May but will be OOO later in the year.
- The Japan engineering lead (Hiro) mentioned Golden Week conflicts in early May — he flagged May 3–5 might be patchy for attendance.
- Our EU team observes the Easter bank holidays in April, so April 4 week is bad for us.

Can you propose a few time options that avoid the named holidays and also work across US/EU/APAC windows? We prefer weekday slots that don't push attendance past 19:00 local for any region.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Rao
Director, Product 
Acme Enterprises

Hi Priya — great to hear from you and thanks for the constraints.

We can absolutely do a short series: an overview for the broader group and a technical deep-dive with infra/ops. To avoid the holiday collisions you called out, two quick notes:
1) Golden Week in Japan typically spans early May; to be safe we avoid May 3–6 for full participation.
2) For cross-region meetings that include US west coast and Japan, there are naturally early mornings / late evenings involved. We try to limit sessions to a 4–6 hour overlap window where possible.

Proposed options (all times shown as UTC for clarity):
- Option A: May 10, 09:00 UTC (overview 60m) — avoids Golden Week and keeps EU and US in reasonable hours.
- Option B: May 11, 14:00 UTC (overview 60m + optional deep-dive later) — later for EU but better for Japan.
- Option C: Split the overview: US/EU session May 9, 16:00 UTC and APAC-focused May 11, 00:30 UTC (shorter, recorded).

Rishi — can you confirm whether we can offer a follow-up deep-dive the same week (two-hour deep technical session) and I'll attach a mutual action plan and a provisional calendar invite once Priya confirms preferred option.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Proposed options + notes on DST/GMT shifts

Kim / Marissa — quick internal note before we lock time with Acme:

- DST transitions: UK/EU will switch to BST end of March; by May the offsets are stable but remember US switches earlier/later depending on region. For scheduling that touches US and EU, the effective overlap moves ~1 hour vs winter — small but noticeable for 18:00 local cutoffs.
- Golden Week impact (Japan): Hiro flagged that while the formal holidays are May 3–5, many teams take extended time May 1–6 for travel; that's why I like May 10/11 ideas rather than early-May slots.
- Diwali: as Priya said, that's an end-of-year OOO — relevant if we try to schedule a follow-up in November.

Suggested approach: propose the May 10 overview (Option A) as the primary, and offer a recorded APAC-friendly split session for those who can't attend. Keep the deep-dive tentatively the week of May 10–14 and ask the infra leads for their 2-hour blocks.

Marissa — can you approve a 2-hour block for Rishi/engineer calendar hold? Also request a small discretionary demo window in our calendar for May 12 06:00 UTC in case APAC needs an ultra-early slot.

Thanks — Rishi
